summary.en: Maduro and his wife have pleaded not guilty to U.S. conspiracy to torture charges, and Maduro is returning to federal court to face the allegations. The United States has lifted sanctions on Jorge Rodríguez, head of Venezuela's National Assembly, easing pressure on opposition leaders. The U.S. Space Force has deployed electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela, mirroring actions in Iran. A ReliefWeb update notes limited purchasing power despite gradual macroeconomic and earthquake recovery. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Maduro og hans kone har erklært seg ikke skyldige i amerikanske konspirasjonsanklager om tortur, og Maduro vender tilbake til føderalt rettsapparat for å møte påstandene. USA har opphevet sanksjonene mot Jorge Rodríguez, leder for Venezuelas nasjonalforsamling, og lettet presset på opposisjonsledere. US Space Force har satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer mot Venezuela, i likhet med handlinger i Iran. En oppdatering fra ReliefWeb bemerker begrenset kjøpekraft til tross for gradvis makroøkonomisk og jordskjelvsgjenoppretting. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
